title: Net to Solid Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Fold the net of a cube, prism, or pyramid into its solid with a slider, and click a face of the net to follow it into place.

educational.topic: Nets of polyhedra and Euler's formula
learningObjectives: Students will be able to explain how a two-dimensional net folds into a three-dimensional solid and identify which face of the net becomes which face of the solid.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Learner-controlled folding with color-matched faces across a 2D and a 3D view
keyQuestions: Which faces of the net share an edge on the solid but not in the net?
Why does the top of the cube travel farther than the other faces?
Does Euler's formula hold for every solid here?
commonMisconceptions: Every arrangement of six squares folds into a cube.
A solid has only one net.
Faces next to each other in the net are the only faces that touch on the solid.
assessmentOpportunities: Students are given three patterns of six squares and decide which fold into a cube, justifying each decision by naming the faces that would overlap or leave a gap.
